text:
Donald Knuth was born in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. His early interest in problem-solving led him to win a contest in eighth grade by identifying over 4,500 words from a given set of letters. He attended the Case Institute of Technology, where he was introduced to the IBM 650, and later switched his focus from physics to mathematics. He received both a Bachelor of Science and a master of science from Case in 1960.
After graduating, Knuth worked as a consultant to Burroughs Corporation and later earned his PhD in mathematics from the California Institute of Technology in 1963. He was a founding editor of the *Case Institute's Engineering and Science Review* . Knuth became deeply involved in computer science, notably developing the FORTRAN compiler and contributing to the creation of ALGOL compilers. He dedicated significant time to writing *The Art of Computer Programming* , which he eventually developed into seven volumes. He also created TeX and Metafont for digital typesetting and developed the concept of literate programming.
